Q: What is the Office of the Tax Ombud?   Drag
A: It is an independent office that reviews and resolves complaints from taxpayers regarding actions or decisions of tax authorities.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: Why was the FIRS replaced with the NRS?
text:
Q: Why was the FIRS replaced with the NRS?
A: The change aims to modernize and strengthen Nigeria's revenue administration framework, expand the scope of revenue collection, improve efficiency, and align with current economic realities and international best practices.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: What are the key functions of the NRS?
text:
Q: What are the key functions of the NRS?
A: Key functions include tax assessment, collection, enforcement, taxpayer education, policy review, international collaboration, data management, fraud detection, and administering all federal revenues.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: Can the NRS collect taxes for states and local governments?
text:
Q: Can the NRS collect taxes for states and local governments?
A: Yes, the NRS may, upon request, assist states, the Federal Capital Territory, or local governments in collecting taxes they are legally empowered to administer, subject to agreed terms.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: Who governs the NRS?
text:
Q: Who governs the NRS?
A: The NRS is governed by a Governing Board comprising the Executive Chairman, Executive Directors of the Service, representatives from key ministries and agencies, and appointed members representing Nigeria’s geopolitical zones

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: How is the Executive Chairman appointed?
text:
Q: How is the Executive Chairman appointed?
A: The Executive Chairman is appointed by the President, subject to confirmation by the Senate, and serves as the chief executive and accounting officer of the Service.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: What happens to FIRS staff and assets?
text:
Q: What happens to FIRS staff and assets?
A: All staff, assets, rights, obligations, and pending matters of the FIRS are transferred to the NRS under terms not less favorable than before.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: Is the NRS tax-exempt?
text:
Q: Is the NRS tax-exempt?
A: Yes, the NRS is exempt from income tax but must still deduct and remit taxes as required by law.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: How does the NRS ensure taxpayer confidentiality?
text:
Q: How does the NRS ensure taxpayer confidentiality?
A: The Act imposes strict confidentiality obligations on NRS officials. Unauthorized disclosure of taxpayer information is a criminal offence punishable by fine or imprisonment.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: How does the NRS handle international tax agreements?
text:
Q: How does the NRS handle international tax agreements?
A: The NRS implements agreements for avoiding double taxation and providing administrative assistance with other countries, including collecting taxes on behalf of foreign governments.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: What penalties exist for non-compliance with tax laws?
text:
Q: What penalties exist for non-compliance with tax laws?
A: The NRS may impose penalties for non-compliance, including fines, prosecution, and seizure of assets derived from tax fraud or evasion.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: How are disputes against the NRS handled?
text:
Q: How are disputes against the NRS handled?
A: Suits against the NRS must be filed within three months of the incident and require one month’s prior written notice. The Public Officers Protection Act applies to such cases.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: What is the role of the NRS Technical Committee?
text:
Q: What is the role of the NRS Technical Committee?
A: The Technical Committee advises the Board on professional and technical tax matters and reviews complex tax issues.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: How does the NRS promote tax compliance?
text:
Q: How does the NRS promote tax compliance?
A: The NRS must submit annual reports and audited accounts to the Minister, who presents them to the Federal Executive Council and National Assembly.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: What is the process for recovering unremitted revenue?
text:
Q: What is the process for recovering unremitted revenue?
A: The Accountant-General of the Federation may deduct unremitted revenues from allocations due to any government agency upon receipt of a warrant from the NRS Executive Chairman and a judicial officer.

document_title: NRS Frequently Asked Questions (nrs.gov.ng)
heading: Where can I get more information about the NRS?
text:
Q: Where can I get more information about the NRS?
A: Official information will be available through the NRS website, public notices, and designated offices once the Service becomes operational.
